habitude.r1_t: A love that's very much alive
habitude.r1_d: Your answers breathe love far more than habit. The early passion may have evolved, but it has given way to a deep attachment, a real desire to share and to choose the other. Your relationship is a source of joy, not just a routine.
habitude.r1_a: Keep nurturing this precious bond: the little gestures, the plans, the moments of closeness and desire. A living love is cultivated every day, and that's clearly what you're already doing.
habitude.r2_t: Love wins, but routine is settling in
habitude.r2_d: The love is there, but routine is starting to nibble at your relationship. That's perfectly normal after a few years: daily life takes over and the little attentions space out. Nothing alarming, but a signal not to let habit smother what you truly feel.
habitude.r2_a: Rekindle the spark on purpose: surprises, one-on-one time, new experiences together. Talk again about your wishes and dreams. Often, simply putting the relationship back at the top of your priorities brings the spark back.
habitude.r3_d: Your answers show that habit now takes up more room than the pull of love. You probably still care about your partner, but the desire, the closeness and the urge to plan ahead have faded. It's not a foregone conclusion, but it calls for real awareness.
habitude.r3_a: Ask yourself honestly: do I want to revive this relationship, or is it mainly fear of change that holds me? If you want to believe in it, working on it together (honest dialogue, couples therapy) can restart the engine. The worst would be to drift without deciding anything.
habitude.r4_t: It's mostly habit that binds you
habitude.r4_d: Based on your answers, it's habit, comfort or fear that hold you far more than love. Desire, closeness and the wish for a shared future seem to have gone out. It doesn't mean all is lost, but the current status quo probably isn't making you happy.
habitude.r4_a: Give yourself real time to reflect, alone and then together. Do you want to try to rebuild something alive, or have you drifted apart for good? There's no shame in asking the question, and support (a psychologist, a couples therapist) can help you see clearly.
habitude.q1: When you're reunited with your partner after a day apart, you feel…
habitude.q1a: Real joy: I want to tell them about my day and share it.
habitude.q1b: Pleasure, a reassuring and comforting presence.
habitude.q1c: Not much in particular; it's become routine.
habitude.q1d: Sometimes weariness, even relief when they're not around.
habitude.q2: Today, your physical attraction to your partner…
habitude.q2a: Is still very much alive: I'm still drawn to them.
habitude.q2b: Has calmed down, but stays real and tender.
habitude.q2c: Has faded a lot; we mostly run on habit.
habitude.q2d: Has almost vanished: I don't even think about it anymore.
habitude.q3: If you had to say why you're still together, it would be above all…
habitude.q3a: Because I love them and I choose this person, every day.
habitude.q3b: Out of love, with the comfort of a settled relationship.
habitude.q3c: Out of habit, and because changing everything is scary.
habitude.q3d: For convenience: logistics, fear of being alone, what others would think.
habitude.q4: When you imagine your life without your partner, you feel…
habitude.q4a: A real emptiness: the thought of losing them aches.
habitude.q4b: Sadness, but I know I'd get through it.
habitude.q4c: A strange mix of apprehension and curiosity.
habitude.q4d: Mostly relief, sometimes even a sense of freedom.
habitude.q5: Do you still make plans together (trips, dreams, the future)?
habitude.q5a: Yes, we still build and dream together with real desire.
habitude.q5c: Rarely; we live day to day, each on our own side.
habitude.q5d: Not really: our futures no longer take shape together.
habitude.q6: Do you still make an effort to please them?
habitude.q6a: Yes, I still love to surprise them and take care of us.
habitude.q6b: Now and then, when the occasion arises.
habitude.q6c: Rarely; we don't really do little gestures anymore.
habitude.q6d: No, we've stopped making an effort for each other.
habitude.q7: Your everyday conversations mostly revolve around…
habitude.q7a: Everything: our feelings, our ideas, our wishes, our days.
habitude.q7b: A good mix of the practical and the personal.
habitude.q7d: The bare minimum; we don't have much left to say.
habitude.q8: When you're apart for a few days, you miss your partner…
habitude.q8a: A lot: I often think of them and can't wait to be back together.
habitude.q8b: Yes, a gentle, quiet kind of missing.
habitude.q8c: A little, but I also enjoy that time for myself.
habitude.q8d: Not really: I actually feel pretty good on my own.
habitude.q9: Do you still feel admiration or pride toward your partner?
habitude.q9a: Yes, I admire them and I'm proud to be with them.
habitude.q9b: Yes, for certain of their qualities.
habitude.q9c: Less and less; I mostly see their flaws.
habitude.q9d: Not at all: their opinion barely matters to me anymore.
habitude.q10: The tender gestures between you (hugs, hands, kisses) are…
habitude.q10a: Spontaneous and frequent: we love to touch.
habitude.q10b: Present, especially at certain moments of the day.
habitude.q10c: Rare and a bit mechanical, out of habit.
habitude.q10d: Almost non-existent: we barely touch anymore.
habitude.q11: If your partner grew close to someone else, you would feel…
habitude.q11a: Real pain: the idea of losing them is unbearable.
habitude.q11b: Jealousy and a lot of hurt.
habitude.q11c: A pang, but weaker than before.
habitude.q11d: Almost indifference, even a way out.
habitude.q12: What holds you most in this relationship is…
habitude.q12a: Love and the desire to continue this story.
habitude.q12b: Love, mixed with the comfort of what we've built.
habitude.q12c: Mostly the fear of starting all over again.
habitude.q12d: The fear of emptiness, loneliness, or others' judgement.
habitude.q13: Do you still laugh together, share moments of closeness?
habitude.q13a: Yes, often: it's one of our greatest strengths.
habitude.q13c: Now and then, but it's rarer than before.
habitude.q14: If you met your partner today, for the first time…
habitude.q14a: I'd fall for them again without hesitation: I'd choose them.
habitude.q14b: I think so; they'd still appeal to me.
habitude.q14c: I'm not sure: maybe we've changed too much.
habitude.q14d: Honestly, no, I wouldn't get together with this person.
habitude.q15: Do you confide in your partner when something moves you?
habitude.q15a: Yes, they're the first person I turn to.
habitude.q15b: Often, though I keep some things to myself.
habitude.q15c: Not much; I tend to confide in others.
habitude.q15d: No: we don't really share our inner lives anymore.
habitude.q16: When you make a compromise or a sacrifice for them, you experience it…
habitude.q16a: With pleasure, because their happiness matters to me.
habitude.q16b: Naturally: it's part of life as a couple.
habitude.q16d: With resentment: I feel I sacrifice for nothing.
habitude.q17: The spark, the butterflies of the early days…
habitude.q17a: Are still there, in a deeper and steadier form.
habitude.q17b: Come back at times, on special occasions.
habitude.q17c: Have faded a lot over time.
habitude.q17d: Have completely gone: everything feels flat.
habitude.q18: Do you still want to discover and understand your partner?
habitude.q18a: Yes, they still surprise and interest me.
habitude.q18b: Yes, even though I think I know them well.
habitude.q18c: Not really: I feel I've seen it all.
habitude.q18d: No: I'm often bored with them.
habitude.q19: The kids, the house, money, what others think… in your couple, these factors…
habitude.q19a: Aren't what binds us: love comes first.
habitude.q19b: Matter, but come after our feelings.
habitude.q19c: Weigh heavily in my decision to stay.
habitude.q19d: Are clearly the main reason I stay.
habitude.q20: Deep down, when you think about your relationship today, you tell yourself…
habitude.q20a: “I truly love them and I'm where I belong.”
habitude.q20b: “We love each other, even if the early passion has changed.”
habitude.q20c: “I care about them, but I'm no longer sure it's love.”
habitude.q20d: “We stay together out of habit, more than out of love.”
